questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that I studied in a country with many opportunities to evolve my English language. I choose Australia since they speak English.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I do not think it was easy, but the University has a help center and a chat.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of help from the student help center on the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I would recommend you stay up late or wake up early so you catch the help centre on the chat at the university's website when they are open. It is a mess trying to contact them by mail with the time difference. It took me around 2 weeks of trying to get answers by mail and about 2 hours to get help on the chat.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It was possible to live close to the university in your own apartment or a room in a shared apartment.
You can choose between premium or standard apartments. The main difference is that there is air-conditioning in the premium room.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a kitchen in the apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It is too expensive because the quality is really poor.
However, it is nice to socialise with all the other students in the Village.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You should only stay there if you want to socialise. Do not do it because it seems cheap. It is possible to live in houses just as cheaply around the area where it is clean:).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I had to choose my courses through a portal at the university. When I was assigned to the courses I needed to choose which classes I would attend.
You plan your own schedule which is pretty cool. I would really recommend placing all of your classes together on 1 or 2 days, so you have more time to travel and experience Australia.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The University had a portal where I could ask for help. However, because of the time difference it is a long process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful. I received the classes and time schedule that i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early. If you cannot figure it out, the university can help you when you arrive so do not stress about it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was okay. It was not that hard so do not stress.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I loved the style of teaching. It is much more practical than the style of teaching at the University of Copenhagen. Furthermore, WSU is really good at offering online solutions if you cannot attend the physical classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Fundamentals of Australian Law, Criminal Law, Contracts, Property Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Contracts, Criminal Law, Property Law.

questions.answer: Food, books and travelling are more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are clubs, but some of them have a long sign-up process so it is not possible to attend them if you are there for only one semester.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are clubs for almost every sport.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I haven't tried any of them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
If you want to travel: Go to Byron Bay, Cairns, Port Douglas, Melbourne.

If you want to do something near Sydney: Go to Royal National park, Blue mountains and of course all of the highlights in Sydney. 

Great tip: Use popcar!! It is like Share now in Denmark and is pretty cheap to rent a car for one or more days. If you sign up as a student the subscription will not cost you anything. 
The cars are placed all over Sydney. There is an app where you can see the cars.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy it is not so different from Europe.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs or live on campus. When living on campus, there is a lot of events and parties to attend.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are all so nice and caring.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be social, Go travel while you are there, and enjoy:). The time flies.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being so independent and not having any obligations.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
